title: Agent Framework Tradeoffs — LangGraph vs CrewAI vs AutoGen vs Agno

questions.question: Your team must choose between plain code, a simple pipeline, or a full workflow engine for a new automation task. What is the sensible way to decide?
options: Match the complexity of the solution to the coordination needs of the task
Always use the most complex framework for every task regardless of need
Always avoid every framework and rewrite everything from scratch each time
Choose the option based only on which name sounds most impressive
questions.explanation: Simple tasks do not need heavy machinery and complex tasks outgrow plain scripts. This lesson builds on that judgment by comparing agent frameworks against concrete task needs.

questions.question: Which signal makes `recommend` choose LangGraph before it considers dialogue or role-based branches?
options: `has_roles=True` with no typed state
Resume, human-interrupt, or parallel-fanout needs
`needs_session_memory=True` with no roles and no dialogue
`has_dialogue=True` with no typed state
questions.explanation: The durable-workflow branch checks resume, human interrupts, and parallel fanout and returns LangGraph immediately. Those features require explicit state, checkpointing, or graph fanout in this decision tree.

questions.question: What recommendation does `Problem(has_dialogue=True, total_llm_calls=10)` receive when `has_typed_state` is false?
options: `plain python`, because dialogue is not a state transition
`autogen`, only if `needs_resume` is also true
`autogen`, because proposer/critic dialogue is its native shape
`crewai`, because every multi-agent conversation is modeled as specialist roles
questions.explanation: After the early LangGraph branch, the code checks `has_dialogue and not has_typed_state` and returns `autogen`. The ten-call count keeps the task out of the small plain-Python shortcut.

questions.question: Why does a `Problem(has_roles=True, total_llm_calls=4)` select CrewAI in the bundled cases?
options: CrewAI is selected for every task with more than two LLM calls, regardless of roles
Roles are ignored unless the task also needs a durable checkpoint
The session-memory branch runs first and maps all role-based tasks to Agno
Specialist roles without typed state match CrewAI's pipeline branch
questions.explanation: The role branch requires `has_roles` and `not has_typed_state`. Four calls avoid the plain-code shortcut, and no earlier resume, interrupt, fanout, or dialogue branch applies.

questions.question: What is the recommendation for `Problem(needs_session_memory=True, total_llm_calls=6)` with no roles or dialogue?
options: `agno`, because the single-agent session-memory branch matches
`langgraph`, because persistent memory is always represented as typed graph state
`plain python`, because session memory is not a workflow feature
`crewai`, because memory implies multiple specialist roles
questions.explanation: With more than two calls and no role/dialogue/typed-state signals, the `needs_session_memory` branch selects Agno for its built-in storage-oriented single-agent shape.

questions.question: If `Problem(has_typed_state=True, total_llm_calls=5)` has no resume, interrupt, fanout, roles, dialogue, or session memory, which fallback applies?
options: `plain python`, because typed state is only an annotation and never affects the tree
`langgraph`, because typed state maps to `StateGraph`
`autogen`, because any unknown case is a dialogue problem
`agno`, because no role signal means a single agent
questions.explanation: The final typed-state check returns LangGraph with a reason to map the `TypedDict` onto a `StateGraph`. The generic fallback is also LangGraph, but this case reaches the typed-state branch explicitly.
